questions.q: If $Z_1$ and $Z_2$ are two non-zero complex numbers, then which of the following is not true?
questions.explanation: The triangle inequality gives |Z1+Z2| ≤ |Z1|+|Z2|, so the reverse inequality stated in option (4) is not generally true.

questions.q: The real value of '$\alpha$' for which $\dfrac{1-i\sin\alpha}{1+2i\sin\alpha}$ is purely real is
questions.explanation: Rationalising, the imaginary part is proportional to $-3\sin\alpha$. For this to vanish, $\sin\alpha=0$, i.e. $\alpha=n\pi,n\in N$.

questions.q: If A.M. and G.M. of roots of a quadratic equation are 5 and 4 respectively, then the quadratic equation is
questions.explanation: $\alpha+\beta=2(5)=10$ and $\alpha\beta=4^2=16$, so the equation is $x^2-(\alpha+\beta)x+\alpha\beta=0$, i.e. $x^2-10x+16=0$.

questions.q: The modulus of the complex number $\dfrac{(1+i)^2(1+3i)}{(2-6i)(2-2i)}$ is
questions.explanation: $(1+i)^2=2i$, numerator $=2i(1+3i)=-6+2i$ with modulus $2\sqrt{10}$; denominator $=(2-6i)(2-2i)=-8-16i$ with modulus $8\sqrt5$. Ratio $=\dfrac{2\sqrt{10}}{8\sqrt5}=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{4}$.

questions.q: If 3x + i(4x - y) = 6 - i where x and y are real numbers, then the values of x and y are respectively,
questions.explanation: Equating real parts: $3x=6\Rightarrow x=2$. Equating imaginary parts: $4x-y=-1\Rightarrow y=9$.

questions.q: If $\left(\dfrac{1+i}{1-i}\right)^{x}=1$ then
questions.explanation: (1+i)/(1-i) = i, and $i^x=1$ requires x to be a multiple of 4, so x = 4n, n$\in$N.

questions.q: If $z=x+iy$, then the equation $|z+1|=|z-1|$ represents
questions.explanation: This is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining $-1$ and $1$, which is the y-axis ($x=0$).

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are roots of the equation $x^2+x+1=0$ then $\alpha^2+\beta^2$ is
questions.explanation: $\alpha+\beta=-1,\ \alpha\beta=1$, so $\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta=1-2=-1$.

If $\left(\dfrac{1+i}{1-i}\right)^m=1$, then the least positive integral value of m is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1+i}{1-i}=i$, and $i^m=1$ needs the least positive $m=4$.

questions.q: The real part of $(1 - \cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^{-1}$ is
questions.explanation: Writing $1-\cos\theta+i\sin\theta=2\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\,i\,e^{-i\theta/2}$ and taking the reciprocal, the real part simplifies to $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.q: The simplified form of $i^n + i^{n+1} + i^{n+2} + i^{n+3}$ is

If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $x^2 - ax + b^2 = 0$, then $\alpha^2 + \beta^2$ is equal to ____
questions.explanation: $\alpha+\beta=a$, $\alpha\beta=b^2$, so $\alpha^2+\beta^2=(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta=a^2-2b^2$.

questions.q: If $1, \omega, \omega^2$ are three cube roots of unity, then $(1-\omega+\omega^2)(1+\omega-\omega^2)$ is ____
questions.explanation: $1-\omega+\omega^2=-2\omega$ and $1+\omega-\omega^2=-2\omega^2$ (using $1+\omega+\omega^2=0$); product $=4\omega^3=4$.

questions.q: If $x$ is real, then the minimum value of $x^2-8x+17$ is ____
questions.explanation: $x^2-8x+17=(x-4)^2+1$, whose minimum value is $1$.

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are two different complex numbers with $|\beta| = 1$, then $\left|\dfrac{\beta-\alpha}{1-\bar\alpha\beta}\right|$ is equal to
questions.explanation: This is a standard identity: whenever $|\beta|=1$, $\left|\dfrac{\beta-\alpha}{1-\bar\alpha\beta}\right|=1$ for any complex $\alpha$.

questions.q: If the roots of the equation $x^3+ax^2+bx+c=0$ are in A.P., then $2a^3-9ab=$
questions.explanation: The middle root equals $-a/3$; substituting into the cubic and simplifying gives $2a^3-9ab=-27c$.

questions.q: The modulus and amplitude of $\dfrac{1+2i}{1-(1-i)^2}$ are
questions.explanation: $(1-i)^2=-2i$, so the expression is $\dfrac{1+2i}{1+2i}=1$, with modulus 1 and amplitude 0.

questions.q: If $2x=-1+\sqrt3i$, then the value of $(1-x^2+x)^6-(1-x+x^2)^6=$
questions.explanation: Here $x$ is a complex cube root of unity satisfying $x^2+x+1=0$; both bracketed expressions reduce to $\mp2x^2,-2x$ whose sixth powers use $x^6=1$, giving the difference 0.

questions.q: If $\alpha$ is a complex number such that $\alpha^2 - \alpha + 1 = 0$, then $\alpha^{2011} =$
questions.explanation: $\alpha$ is a primitive 6th root of unity ($\alpha^6=1$). Since $2011=6\times335+1$, $\alpha^{2011}=\alpha$.

questions.q: If the conjugate of $(x + iy)(1 - 2i)$ is $1 + i$, then
questions.explanation: $(x+iy)(1-2i)=\overline{1+i}=1-i$, so $x+iy=\dfrac{1-i}{1-2i}=\dfrac{3}{5}+\dfrac{1}{5}i$, giving $x=3/5,\ y=1/5$.

questions.q: If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are the roots of the equation $x^3 + 4x + 2 = 0$, then $\alpha^3 + \beta^3 + \gamma^3 =$
questions.explanation: Here $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=0$, $\alpha\beta\gamma=-2$. When the sum of the roots is zero, $\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3=3\alpha\beta\gamma=-6$.

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are different complex numbers with $|\beta| = 1$, then $\left|\dfrac{\beta-\alpha}{1-\bar\alpha\beta}\right|$ is equal to
questions.explanation: This is a standard identity: whenever $|\beta|=1$, $\left|\dfrac{\beta-\alpha}{1-\bar\alpha\beta}\right|=1$.

questions.q: The number of solutions of the equation $z^2 + \bar z = 0$ where $z \in C$ are
questions.explanation: Writing $z=x+iy$ and separating real and imaginary parts gives $y=0$ (with $x=0,-1$) or $x=1/2$ (with $y=\pm\sqrt3/2$), a total of 4 solutions.

questions.q: If $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ are roots of $x^3-2x+1=0$, then the value of $\displaystyle\sum\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha+\beta-\gamma}\right)$ is ...........
questions.explanation: $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=0$ so $\alpha+\beta-\gamma=-2\gamma$. The sum becomes $-\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha}+\dfrac{1}{\beta}+\dfrac{1}{\gamma}\right)=-\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha}{\alpha\beta\gamma}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\cdot\dfrac{-2}{-1}=-1$.

questions.q: The value of $\left|\dfrac{1+i\sqrt3}{\left(1+\dfrac{1}{i+1}\right)^2}\right|$ is ............
questions.explanation: $1+\dfrac{1}{i+1}=\dfrac{3-i}{2}$, whose square is $\dfrac{4-3i}{2}$. Then $\left|\dfrac{1+i\sqrt3}{(4-3i)/2}\right|=\dfrac{2\times2}{5}=\dfrac45$.

questions.q: If $\omega$ is an imaginary cube root of unity, then the value of $(1-\omega+\omega^2)\cdot(1-\omega^2+\omega^4)\cdot(1-\omega^4+\omega^8)\cdot...........(2n\text{ factors})$ is ............
questions.explanation: Each pair of factors simplifies to $(-2\omega)(-2\omega^2)=4\omega^3=4$; with $n$ such pairs among $2n$ factors, the product is $4^n=2^{2n}$.

questions.q: If $P(x,y)$ denotes $z=x+iy$ in Argand's plane and $\left|\dfrac{z-1}{z+2i}\right|=1$, then the locus of $P$ is a/an .........................
questions.explanation: $|z-1|=|z+2i|$ means $P$ is equidistant from $(1,0)$ and $(0,-2)$, so the locus is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them, a straight line.

questions.q: In Argand's plane, the point corresponding to $\dfrac{(1-i\sqrt3)(1+i)}{(\sqrt3+i)}$ lies in ............
questions.explanation: Simplifying the expression gives $1-i$, which corresponds to the point $(1,-1)$, lying in quadrant IV.

questions.q: If $a$, $-a$, $b$ are the roots of $x^3-5x^2-x+5=0$, then $b$ is a root of
questions.explanation: Sum of products in pairs $=-a^2=-1\Rightarrow a^2=1$; product of roots $=-a^2b=-5\Rightarrow b=5$. Checking, $x=5$ satisfies $x^2-3x-10=0$.

questions.q: The least positive integer $n$, for which $\dfrac{(1+i)^n}{(1-i)^{n-2}}$ is positive, is
questions.explanation: Since $(1-i)^2=-2i$ and $(1+i)/(1-i)=i$, the expression equals $-2i^{n+1}$; at $n=1$ this is $-2i^2=2$, a positive real number, so the least such $n$ is $1$.

questions.q: If $x+iy=(-1+i\sqrt3)^{2010}$, then $x=$
questions.explanation: $-1+i\sqrt3=2\,\text{cis}(120^\circ)$, so raising to the $2010$th power gives $2^{2010}\text{cis}(2010\times120^\circ)=2^{2010}\text{cis}(0^\circ)=2^{2010}$, purely real.

questions.q: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $x^2 + x + 1 = 0$, then $\alpha^{16} + \beta^{16} =$
questions.explanation: $\alpha,\beta$ are the complex cube roots of unity $\omega,\omega^2$. Since $\omega^3=1$, $\omega^{16}=\omega$ and $\omega^{32}=\omega^2$, so the sum is $\omega+\omega^2=-1$.

questions.q: The complex number $\dfrac{1+2i}{1-i}$ lies in
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1+2i}{1-i} = \dfrac{(1+2i)(1+i)}{2} = \dfrac{-1+3i}{2}$, which has negative real part and positive imaginary part, so it lies in the second quadrant.

questions.q: If P is the point in the Argand diagram corresponding to the complex number $\sqrt3 + i$ and if OPQ is an isosceles right angled triangle, right angled at 'O', then Q represents the complex number
questions.explanation: Since $OQ=OP$ and $\angle POQ = 90^\circ$, Q is P rotated by $\pm90^\circ$ about O, i.e. $P$ multiplied by $\pm i$: $i(\sqrt3+i)=-1+i\sqrt3$ or $-i(\sqrt3+i)=1-i\sqrt3$.

questions.q: The smallest positive integral value of 'n' such that $\left[\dfrac{1+\sin\frac{\pi}{8}+i\cos\frac{\pi}{8}}{1+\sin\frac{\pi}{8}-i\cos\frac{\pi}{8}}\right]^n$ is purely imaginary is, n =
questions.explanation: Writing $\sin(\pi/8)=\cos(3\pi/8)$ and $\cos(\pi/8)=\sin(3\pi/8)$, the bracket simplifies to $e^{i\cdot3\pi/8}$, so the expression is $e^{i\,3n\pi/8}$; this is purely imaginary when $3n\pi/8$ is an odd multiple of $\pi/2$, first satisfied at $n=4$.
